checks.context: Without control plane logs (api, audit, authenticator, controllerManager, scheduler), you have no visibility into who accessed the Kubernetes API or what changes were made. The audit log is particularly important for incident response and compliance.

Without envelope encryption, Kubernetes secrets (which often contain database passwords, API keys, and TLS certs) are stored in etcd in base64 only - not encrypted. Use a KMS key to encrypt secrets at rest.

checks.message: EKS API server endpoint publicly accessible
checks.context: By default, the EKS API server endpoint is publicly accessible from the entire Internet (0.0.0.0/0). Any credential leak or API server vulnerability is immediately exploitable from anywhere. Restrict access using publicAccessCidrs or disable public access entirely with endpointPublicAccess=false,endpointPrivateAccess=true.

checks.message: EKS authentication mode defaults to CONFIG_MAP
checks.context: CONFIG_MAP authentication relies on the aws-auth ConfigMap, a well-known attack surface where a single misconfiguration can grant cluster-admin. API and API_AND_CONFIG_MAP modes use EKS access entries which are more auditable and manageable via IAM.

checks.message: Deletion protection disabled — cluster can be permanently deleted with a single command
checks.context: Without deletion protection, a single eks delete-cluster command permanently removes the entire cluster and all its workloads. Enable deletion protection for production clusters.

checks.message: Verify endpoint access settings are not being made more permissive
checks.context: Enabling public endpoint access without IP restrictions exposes the Kubernetes API server to the entire internet. Brute-force and credential stuffing attacks against the API server are common.

checks.message: Ensure node IAM role follows least-privilege
checks.context: Node group IAM roles are attached to every EC2 instance in the group. Overly permissive roles mean a compromised pod can access the instance metadata service and steal the node's credentials.

checks.message: Disk size not set — default may be insufficient for workloads
checks.context: Nodes running out of disk space can cause pod evictions and cluster instability. Specify an appropriate disk size for your workloads.

checks.message: EKS cluster deletion is permanent - all workloads will be terminated
checks.context: Deleting an EKS cluster terminates all node groups and running pods. Persistent volumes (EBS) may be deleted depending on the reclaim policy. Ensure all critical data is backed up before proceeding.

checks.message: Verify OIDC provider configuration before associating
checks.context: Misconfigured OIDC identity providers can allow unintended principals to authenticate to your cluster. Verify the issuer URL, client ID, and username/groups claims are correctly scoped.

checks.message: Addon updates can cause brief disruption - verify compatibility with your cluster version
checks.context: Critical addons like vpc-cni, kube-proxy, and coredns affect cluster networking. An incompatible version can break pod networking or DNS resolution across the entire cluster. Test in a non-production cluster first.

checks.message: Kubernetes version upgrades are irreversible - you cannot downgrade
checks.context: The upgrade modifies the control plane and may deprecate APIs your workloads depend on. Verify all addons, node groups, and manifests are compatible with the target version before upgrading.
